summary: At the December 2, 2025 regular meeting of the Allen Township Trustees, attorney Cindy Land from the Hancock County Prosecutor's Office briefed the Trustees on a legal action filed by One Power Company against the Hancock County Board of Elections concerning ballot language for the Allen Township Zoning Resolution. Judge Jonathan P. Starn issued a Decision and Order (Case No. 2025 CV 00168) on November 4, 2025, ruling the May 6, 2025 Primary Election results regarding the Proposed Allen Township Zoning Plan invalid and void, returning Allen Township to unzoned status. The Board of Elections has filed an appeal and a stay on the ruling, and the Proposed Zoning Plan is ordered to be placed on the May 5, 2026 Primary Election ballot with corrected summary language. All zoning certificates issued July through October 2025 were declared unwarranted and associated fees are being returned.
corridor_relevance: The meeting connects to the subject "one_power" solely because One Power Company filed a complaint (Case No. 2025 CV 00168) against the Hancock County Board of Elections asserting that certified ballot language for the Allen Township Zoning Resolution was incorrect and misleading; the minutes do not name any project, site, or purpose associated with One Power Company beyond this legal filing.

summary: During the March 26, 2026 Hancock County Commissioners meeting, Deb Stacy raised concerns about the county commissioners' limited role in economic development, prompting discussion about annexations, utilities, and data centers.
